scope: Four missing conscientious war resisters with actual US military imprisonment; preserve uncertainty and distinguish sentence, jail time, release and discharge.

ctr-roster.label: Courage to Resist, Profiles in Resistance, Klemkewicz and Brobeck entries. Roster used cautiously: identified date conflicts are not copied.

katherine-interview.label: Chris Lombardi, Women’s eNews, August 7, 2006, Conscientious Objector Re-Engineers Her Life; interview in Miramar brig and after release.

katherine-nr.label: Nuclear Resister 142, July 24, 2006, p.1; sentencing May 23 and actual release July 9. The article incorrectly names Iraq; the direct interview establishes Afghanistan.

tony-trial.label: Sarah Lazare, ZNetwork, November 22, 2008, Tony Anderson; trial statements and removal under guard following November 17 court-martial.

tony-custody.label: Courage to Resist prison-support notice reproduced September 10, 2009 by Adopt Resistance; Anthony Michael Anderson/Tony Anderson in Fort Sill custody. November release was an estimate.

tony-release.label: Courage to Resist release announcement quoted October 22, 2009 by The Common Ills; public original HTML retrieved. Freedom confirmed, exact release day not stated.

ivan-wright.label: Ann Wright, Another US War Resister From Canada Court-Martialed, August 24, 2008; November 2006 surrender, December 5 trial, eight-month sentence and February 2007 actual release.

ryan-custody.label: Courage to Resist, Free Ryan Jackson now, May 28, 2008 update; Charleston Naval Brig pretrial custody since April 14.

ryan-trial.label: Nuclear Resister 149, July 3, 2008, p.2 and prison letter; May 30 unauthorized-absence conviction and 100-day sentence. June release was prospective.

prisoner.name: Joel Klemkewicz
prisoner.description: Joel Klemkewicz was a US Marine combat engineer whose religious objections led him to refuse armed duty. After imprisonment, he studied for the ministry and served an Adventist congregation in Okinawa.

cases.charges: Military refusal of duties on religious grounds; exact court-martial specifications unresolved
cases.sentence: The resistance archive reports a December 2004 court-martial and seven-month sentence. His church later reported four months actually imprisoned for refusing Sabbath work. These accounts describe different aspects of his conscientious refusal; the exact specifications and custody endpoints remain unresolved. A later discharge upgrade is not a jail-release date.

case_research.custody_evidence: His denominational publication explicitly confirms four months of imprisonment followed by release and ministerial training; the resistance archive identifies the US Marine proceeding.

entries.custody_evidence: His denominational publication explicitly confirms four months of imprisonment followed by release and ministerial training; the resistance archive identifies the US Marine proceeding.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. Four months is documented actual time, not inferred from the seven-month sentence. No prison-entry year or location is inferred from sentencing or his earlier Okinawa posting. The photograph caption spells Klenkewicz while the article heading spells Klemkewicz; both names screened. No claim that he opposed deployment itself: he reportedly offered to deploy without a weapon.

photo.identity_evidence: Single portrait beneath the named Joel Klemkewicz article on printed page16; caption Pr. Joel Klenkewicz. Embedded image Im4 decoded from original PDF, native234x194, no generative edits or resizing.

prisoner.name: Katherine Jashinski
prisoner.description: Katherine Jashinski was a Texas Army National Guard member who publicly sought conscientious-objector status and refused weapons training for service in Afghanistan. She was imprisoned at the Miramar brig and returned to Texas after release.

cases.charges: Disobeying a superior officer; acquitted of missing movement by design
cases.sentence: Sentenced May 23, 2006 to 120 days, with credit for pretrial confinement, and sent to military prison near San Diego. A reporter visited her at Miramar and confirmed her release on July 9, 2006. The reported 47 days remaining after credit are not the full sentence or a separately added period. The earlier Fort Benning restriction is not given invented prison endpoints.

case_research.custody_evidence: Direct prison interview followed by an actual release interview confirms sustained imprisonment; the contemporary newsletter independently names sentencing and release.

entries.custody_evidence: Direct prison interview followed by an actual release interview confirms sustained imprisonment; the contemporary newsletter independently names sentencing and release.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. Afghanistan is established by the interview; Iraq in the newsletter is an error. Exact Miramar arrival day and nature of all earlier pretrial restrictions remain unresolved. Birth year is not inferred from conflicting reported ages. Named article-photo URL returned 404, so no image bytes shipped.

prisoner.name: Ivan Brobeck
prisoner.description: Ivan Brobeck was a Marine who opposed returning to Iraq after serving there in 2004. He went to Canada, later returned to the United States and was imprisoned following a military prosecution.

cases.charges: Unauthorized absence and missing military movement
cases.sentence: Returned to US authorities in November 2006. Court-martialed December 5, 2006; Ann Wright reports an eight-month sentence and actual release in February 2007. The support archive confirms imprisonment at Quantico. Other summaries give a different sentence, so no full term or exact number of days served is entered.

case_research.custody_evidence: The individual retrospective reports actual release after court-martial imprisonment, corroborated by the resistance organization roster.

entries.custody_evidence: The individual retrospective reports actual release after court-martial imprisonment, corroborated by the resistance organization roster.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. Roster November 2007 return followed by February 2007 release is impossible; Wright gives November 2006. An exact November commitment day is not established. February 6 and 63 days appear in derivative summaries without sufficiently verified primary backing and are withheld. Eight versus ten months and discharge classification conflicts are recorded rather than silently resolved.

prisoner.name: Ryan Jackson
prisoner.description: Ryan Jackson was a US Army private who sought release from military service on conscientious grounds before deployment to Iraq. He joined antiwar organizing and wrote publicly from the Charleston Naval Brig.

cases.charges: Multiple unauthorized absences preceding conscientious-objector application
cases.sentence: Held in pretrial confinement after returning to Fort Gordon on April 14, 2008. Convicted May 30 and sentenced to 100 days with credit for custody already served. A later interview-based book confirms that he was released after the credited term. The contemporary expectation of a late-June release is not copied as an exact endpoint.

case_research.custody_evidence: Contemporary brig correspondence and the later retrospective establish actual pretrial imprisonment and subsequent release.

entries.custody_evidence: Contemporary brig correspondence and the later retrospective establish actual pretrial imprisonment and subsequent release.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. April 4 surrender at Fort Sill and April 14 confinement after return to Fort Gordon are distinct events. AWOL is identified in contemporary charges and conviction reporting; derivative tables saying desertion are not followed. Later book supports release but no precise day is calculated from its 29-day statement. No birthdays or photographs of athlete namesakes are used.
